newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt charges Brotherhood members with incitement.
newsitem.headline: Egypt charges Brotherhood members with incitement.

text.p: Egyptian police have arrested eight suspected members of the Moslem Brotherhood, the largest Islamic political group in Egypt, and charged them with political offences, government newspapers said on Thursday.

The men, who were rounded up on Wednesday, face charges including membership of an outlawed organisation, distributing Brotherhood leaflets and inciting people to participate in demonstrations, the papers said.
The public prosecutor has charged seven other men on the run with the same offences.
"Later in the evening the public prosecutor ordered eight people remanded for 15 days and five released," the daily al-Ahram said. It did not say if the five were also charged.
"These are lies and sheer fabrications," Brotherhood spokesman Mamoun Hudaibi told Reuters.
"Some of them are members but the others are not," he said. "They were arrested to keep out of current elections in the labour unions," he added.
Interior Ministry officials declined to comment.
The papers said police found large quantities of leaflets and Brotherhood literature in the houses of the men.
"There were no leaflets at all with them," Hudaibi said. "Their only fault is that they carry out labour activities and were qualified to win the elections."
The group is reported to be intensifying its activities in the south Cairo industrial suburbs of Helwan and Tebeen.
Most of the detainees are technicians and engineers working at big state-owned factories in the area.
A military court jailed 54 Brotherhood members last year on charges including organising an illegal group, holding illegal secret meetings and preparing anti-government leaflets.
Police rounded up dozens of Brotherhood members and supporters in the run-up to parliamentary elections in November last year.
The Brotherhood advocates the establishment of an Islamic state through elections and other non-violent means but the government has accused it of being a front for militant groups.
